run_metadata.coverage_summary: DEGRADED RUN — FOURTH CONSECUTIVE egress outage (same condition as 2026-10-21, -22 and -23). The execution environment's network policy blocks ALL outbound HTTPS: WebFetch returns getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every host (it does not route via the agent proxy), and the agent proxy itself answers 403 to every CONNECT — confirmed this run via curl against BOTH example.com:443 and www.tenders.gov.au:443 (recentRelayFailures: connect_rejected / 'gateway answered 403 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)'). Per the proxy README a 403 CONNECT is a policy denial that must be reported, not routed around. So NO tender portal, detail page or specification document could be opened on any tier. The only working external channel is WebSearch (routed via Anthropic infrastructure, outside the blocked egress path), which returns titles/URLs/model-summarised snippets dominated by stale cached data (mostly mid-2026, largely closed listings) and cannot read JavaScript-rendered live portals (buy.nsw, tenders.vic, QTenders, NT QTOL), follow pagination, or open attachments. Tier 1 (AusTender + state/territory portals), Tier 2 (VendorPanel public tenders, councils, GBE water corporations, universities) and Tier 3 (SAP Business Network Discovery, major-buyer portals) were all ATTEMPTED via WebSearch only. No fresh (last-7-day) opportunity could be confirmed on any buyer-originated portal this run, and no corporate RFx was publicly visible. The 5 currently-open opportunities previously captured on 2026-10-16..20 (when WebFetch still worked) are carried forward at headline level because their published closing dates (2026-11-12 .. 2026-12-11) all remain in the future as at 2026-10-26. ONE genuinely new source was found this run despite the outage: Landcom (NSW Government land/property developer, a government business enterprise) has launched its own custom-built tender portal — not previously in the known source set. Two apparently-fresh Tier 1 leads surfaced in a WebSearch summary (Victoria RFT 'T2026-0812' DEECA property-portfolio cleaning, close 2026-12-10; ACT 'SL20260630' Suburban Land Agency Kingston land, close 2026-12-01) but could NOT be independently corroborated (a targeted follow-up search returned no matching record and the live portals were unreachable), so they are recorded as unverified leads in gaps, NOT as tenders, to avoid fabrication.
gaps: CRITICAL TOOLING OUTAGE (4th consecutive run; unchanged from 2026-10-21, -22 and -23): outbound HTTPS is blocked by the environment's network policy. WebFetch returns getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every host (it does not use the agent proxy); curl via the agent proxy returns 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. Verified this run via the proxy status endpoint: recentRelayFailures records connect_rejected 403 for BOTH example.com:443 AND www.tenders.gov.au:443, i.e. the denial is universal, not host-specific. Per the proxy README a 403 CONNECT is a policy denial that must be reported, not routed around. No live tender portal, detail page or document could be opened on any tier.

Because detail pages were unreachable, NO deliverables / requirements / evaluation-criteria / document / contact extraction was possible this run. All 5 tenders are headline-level only (counted in entries_pending_detail); their fields derive from prior runs (2026-10-16..20) and must be re-verified on the live portals once egress is restored.

WebSearch index is stale: queries for Oct/Nov/Dec-2026 closings on every Tier 1 portal returned predominantly mid-2026 (closed) listings or platform/landing/help pages. Exhaustive Tier 1 coverage was NOT achieved this run.

Tier 1 state portals (buy.nsw, tenders.vic, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA/SA/TAS, NT QTOL, Tenders ACT) are JavaScript-rendered; WebSearch snippets showed only cached shells, so current open-tender lists were not visible.

UNVERIFIED LEADS (NOT recorded as tenders to avoid fabrication): a WebSearch summary of tenders.vic.gov.au reported an open Victorian RFT 'T2026-0812' (DEECA Property Portfolio Cleaning Services, UNSPSC 76111500, opened 2026-10-08, close 2026-12-10 2:00pm) and an ACT RFT 'SL20260630' (Suburban Land Agency, Kingston Section 49 Block AAb, released 2026-06-30, close 2026-12-01 2:00pm). A targeted follow-up search for 'T2026-0812' returned no matching record (only unrelated UK notices), and neither live portal could be opened to confirm the ID, buyer, scope or dates. They are logged here as leads to verify on the live portals once egress is restored, not captured as opportunities.

None of the 5 carried-forward tenders could be independently re-confirmed on their live portals this run (egress blocked). They are carried forward solely on the basis of their previously-captured, still-open published closing dates (GPSnet EOI DOT46088 closes 2026-11-20; WorkCover occupational rehab FOL26-3030 2026-11-30; Latrobe Regional Health payroll RFQ2262 2026-11-18; ACT Healthy Waterways PICE0014602 2026-11-12; Ports Victoria Station Pier T421508 2026-12-11).

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Business Network Discovery, EstimateOne, BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside/Santos, Woolworths/Coles, Qantas and NFP/health supplier portals are registration/login-gated and/or not readable via WebSearch; no publicly-visible corporate RFx could be confirmed. No corporate opportunities were invented. These portals remain recorded in prior discovered_sources.

The Landcom 'Tallawong TW6' invitation-to-tender surfaced only on a paid aggregator (australiantenders.com.au), used here as a discovery signal only; Landcom's own portal could not be reached (egress blocked) to confirm it, so it is NOT recorded as a tender. Only the Landcom source itself (buyer-originated) is recorded, in discovered_sources.
Invitation-only corporate RFx (e.g. management-consultancy RFPs) remain out of scope and were not fabricated.
De-duplication: the 5 carried-forward tenders reuse their existing dedup_keys and retain their original first_seen dates (2026-10-17..20); the aggregator folds by min-date so lineage is preserved.
recommended_seed_additions: Landcom (NSW Government land and property development organisation; a government business enterprise) — https://www.landcom.com.au — has launched its own custom-built tender portal (developed by UnDigital) and advertises live invitations to tender (e.g. a Tallawong site package on behalf of Sydney Metro). Buyer-originated, not previously in the known source set. Recommend adding to the permanent Tier 2 / gov-business-enterprise source list and resolving the exact portal URL once egress is restored.

OPERATIONAL (not a tender source): This routine has now been unable to reach any live portal for FOUR consecutive runs (2026-10-21/22/23/26). The environment network policy is denying all outbound CONNECTs (403) and WebFetch DNS. The routine cannot perform its core job (open buyer portals and extract deliverables) until the environment is reconfigured with outbound HTTPS access to the tender-portal hosts (or an allow-list added). Human action required: review the environment's network policy at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.

discovered_sources.how_discovered: Source-discovery hunt via WebSearch. Trade press (UnDigital / Campaign Brief / Mumbrella) reports that Landcom, the NSW Government's land and property development organisation (a government business enterprise, formerly UrbanGrowth NSW), has launched its own custom-built digital tender portal (document consolidation, date/time stamping of downloads, question logging). A live Landcom invitation-to-tender (Tallawong TW6, on behalf of Sydney Metro) was visible via a paid aggregator, used here only as a discovery signal. Not previously present in this routine's known source set (zero prior hits for 'Landcom' in the aggregate).
discovered_sources.notes: Genuinely new buyer-originated Tier 2 source. The exact tender-portal URL could NOT be verified this run because outbound HTTPS is blocked (4th consecutive egress outage) — landcom.com.au is the organisation site; resolve and record the dedicated portal endpoint once egress is restored. Landcom is also a NSW Government entity, so some opportunities may additionally appear on buy.nsw eTendering. The Tallawong TW6 opportunity is NOT recorded as a tender because it was seen only on a paid aggregator and could not be confirmed on Landcom's own source this run.
